name: Reinhard Heydrich
role: Chief of the Reich Security Main Office (1939-1942) and Deputy Reich Protector of Bohemia and Moravia (1941-1942)
summary: Nazi security chief who built the Gestapo and SD and organised the Einsatzgruppen and the deportation and murder of European Jews. His own writings and speeches set out a racial-struggle worldview, hostility to Jews, Freemasons, churches and Bolshevism, and plans to Germanise and expel Czechs, with total police power in the Protectorate.

unions-good.rationale: Listed trade unions with parties as organisations of the opponent whose destruction was the first success of the movement; in Prague labour was reorganised under the German Labour Front.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Describes the security police task as 'systematic scanning of all areas of life for enemy influences' and set up index-card surveillance; the stated targets were enemies of the regime, which includes the 'terror groups' he named in 1941.

strong-leader.rationale: In his 1935 pamphlet he credits the Leader with creating national unity, and in his 2 Oct 1941 speech he demands that Prague policy be steered centrally by the Fuehrer's will, over Gau and ministry competences.

state-harmful.rationale: Inferred: from his insistence that the state apparatus, bureaucracy and SS-police must be strong and lead the ideological struggle, he regarded the state as necessary.

empower-police-military.rationale: He built the Gestapo, SD and later the RSHA into the regime's main instruments and in 1941 described the SS as the party's 'Stosstrupp' that must be especially well armed and ready to fight.

decide-locally.rationale: Insisted on central steering of the Protectorate and rejected Gau-level variations in treating Czechs.

more-religion-public.rationale: Said the churches' political and social activity (Catholic Action, schooling) was an anti-state abuse and that their kingdom is 'not of this world'.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Told SS men to expand their knowledge of ancestors, folklore and 'true historical past' and called for it to be passed on.

one-party-rule.rationale: In 1941 said the basic line in the Protectorate 'can only be National Socialist' and called the SS the party's shock troop; in 1935 he treated the banning of all non-Nazi organisations as the first goal achieved.

right-to-secede.rationale: Treated Czech independence aims as a 'stab in the back' to the Reich and defended Bohemia-Moravia as part of the Reich's unity.

natural-rulers.rationale: Said Germans must play the leading role as 'masters in the house' and that Slavs expect the master not to mix with them; praised the 'stronger, noble, racially superior'.

political-violence-never.rationale: Advocated and organised political violence: his 1941 speech endorses shooting and expelling opponents and his 1935 pamphlet says the enemy must be destroyed or Germany will perish.

separate-church-state.rationale: No recorded position. He said the churches should keep out of politics but did not address strict separation of religion and the state.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Said the Bohemian-Moravian space must never be left so that Czechs can call it theirs and must be made 'definitively German'; Wannsee aimed at removing Jews from the living space of the German people.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Presented the main struggle as racial, between the superior and 'subhumans', with Marxism a creation of Jewry.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Stated that the Reich's overall interest comes first and personal interest second, and criticised Germans in the Protectorate who 'only had their purse in view'.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Ended his 1941 address stating a Nazi knows the Reich's overall interest is primary and personal interest comes only after it.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Insisted that the basic line in the Protectorate 'can only be National Socialist', yet set tactical measures by their usefulness to the war effort.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Called Bolshevism a 'brutal destructive domination' by subhumans and a creation of Jewry.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Held that inherited racial 'blood' determines character and ability: ranked Estonians, Latvians and Lithuanians by race and spoke of the Slav's nature in 1941.

total-state.rationale: His 1935 pamphlet calls for 'spiritual and ideological winning of all' areas of national life (art, science, economy); in the Protectorate his regime reorganised labour, closed Czech cultural avenues and planned racial examination of youth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: In 1941 described occupied space as meant to be permanently held, German settlement pushed east 'to the Urals', and a Greater Germanic Reich as the war aim.

national-self-determination.rationale: Said the basic line in the Protectorate was 'combating all Czech independence' and that Czechs have 'nothing left to lose' there; rejected self-rule for Poles and Ukrainians too.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: His 21 Sept 1939 order concentrated Jews in ghettos and barred them from parts of cities; the Wannsee protocol builds the Final Solution on the Nuremberg Laws' racial classification.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Attacked the churches for trying to 'sabotage the sterilization law', which shows support for the law on hereditary disease.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The Gestapo Law he supported placed Gestapo actions beyond court review; he demanded no mitigating circumstances for those who fail to be hard.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Inferred: from his demand that police, SS and state direct national life ideologically, not limited to defence and justice.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Wrote in 1935 that racial mixture with Jews undermined host peoples, and at Wannsee proposed treating half-Jews as Jews and sterilising or dissolving mixed marriages.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Described peoples as ranked in an eternal struggle between the 'racially superior' and 'subhumans' and said Slavs should serve as helots for Germans.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Told officials in 1941 that the Czechs would not be won over: 'we do not want that', only compelled into quiet.

population-transfer.rationale: Planned in 1941 to push out the 'bad race, bad disposition' Czechs to the East ('there is plenty of room'), and organised the deportation of Jews to the East (Wannsee, 1942).

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Masterminded the 1939 Gleiwitz false-flag attack used as a pretext to invade Poland and organised the Einsatzgruppen.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Opens his 1935 pamphlet stating that the life of peoples consists of eternal struggle between the stronger and the weaker.

separated-powers.rationale: As Gestapo chief he put police action beyond court review and as Deputy Protector left President Hácha and the Czech cabinet powerless.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Under his martial law, strikes, sabotage and slow work were treated as resistance and punished by executions.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Wrote that peoples who accepted Jewish immigration and racial mixture were undermined and said Bohemia must be left only German.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: On arrival in Prague he proclaimed martial law, with 142 executions in five days and summary courts; in 1935 he wrote that enemies must be fought without exceptions even at the cost of being condemned as 'brutes'.

party-controls-media.rationale: Stated that any press order he issues must be written up 'without grumbling' as he requires, and that press wording about resistance is chosen for propaganda effect.

clerical-rule.rationale: Called a 'worldly and politically ambitious priesthood' a main enemy of the state and said it fights for secular domination of Germany.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Condemned Czech resistance as a renewed 'stab in the back' against the Reich in wartime.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Said Slavs do not want equal treatment, that goodness is read as weakness, and that Ukrainians should not be given cultural strengthening; contrasts Nordic with 'subhuman'.

death-penalty.rationale: Praised the death sentence on Czech premier Eliáš as a 'masterpiece', ordered executions under martial law, and stated that some Czech leaders would have to be 'put against the wall'.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Held Bohemia-Moravia to be permanently part of the Reich and told officials that the 'reality of belonging to the Reich' must be accepted by Czechs.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Denounced 'political misuse of the churches' and claimed the clergy should limit themselves to being intermediaries not of this world; the SD he led surveilled church activity.

character-from-environment.rationale: Said innate racial nature shapes Czechs and Slavs, yet allowed that Czechs of good race could be re-educated and Germanised.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Said Norway, Holland, Flanders and later Denmark and Sweden, 'of our blood', would belong to a Greater Germanic Reich in some form of federation or Gau.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Closed Czech cultural and patriotic organisations in 1942 and said Czech cultural strengthening should not be encouraged.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Stated that organisations are nothing without the 'forces that give spirit to ideas' and that spiritual forces drive the struggle.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Wrote that world Jewry and Freemasonry are the permanent driving forces of the enemy and that Jews aim at world domination and destruction of the Nordic peoples.

defeat-communism.rationale: Described the war as the 'fateful struggle against Bolshevism' and in 1935 said Bolshevism must be defeated or Germany would perish.

majority-settlement.rationale: Stated that Danzig-West Prussia, the Warthegau, the Baltics and Bohemia-Moravia must be settled by Germans piece by piece so the Polish and Czech element is pushed out.

holocaust-denial.rationale: No recorded position. He organised the deportations and killings; the statement concerns later historical accounts, which he could not address.

suppress-opposition.rationale: In 1941 he reported the 'beating down' of Czech resistance groups and the 'liquidation and removal' of the leading stratum; the Gestapo he led outlawed opposition organisations.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Inferred: from his statement that SS men should provide the best recruits to the armed forces and from his war aims.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The Gestapo law he helped shape removed court review and permitted detention without judicial proceedings; he ruled the Protectorate by decree and summary courts.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Built the Gestapo, concentration-camp system and RSHA as instruments of state security.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Said SS members should be a 'small link between the illustrious cultural past of our folk and the coming thousands of years of Germanic-folkish history'.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Wrote that the struggle had moved to a 'fight of the spirits', that ideological opponents can only be defeated in 'spiritual struggle', and that the enemy is 'spiritual forces'.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Schnellbrief of 1939 demands 'prompt Aryanization' of Jewish enterprises, and Wannsee lists expelling Jews from every sphere of German life.

independent-unions.rationale: Treated unions as enemy organisations to be broken and reorganised the Czech workforce on the German Labour Front model.

racial-pride.rationale: Urged SS men to deepen the 'good elements of our German genetic heritage' and to learn the values of 'our blood, our kind'.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Staged the Gleiwitz pretext for the invasion of Poland and in 1941 described conquered space as to be held and settled permanently.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Said that Germany's enemies, led by Jews and Freemasons, aimed to make Germany 'small and broken'.

sacred-nation.rationale: Presented the folk as continuing across millennia and gave SS members the duty of being a link in its history, which gives individual lives meaning through it.

public-service-media.rationale: Ordered that the Czech press print what he required and managed propaganda lines centrally.

race-social-construct.rationale: Treated race as a biological fact of blood and ordered racial-völkisch surveys of the Czech population using X-ray units and school examinations to sort people.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Repeatedly named the folk's 'blood, spirit and soil' bound strengths as what the enemy tries to destroy.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: In 1941 praised the Fuehrer's transfer of half a million Volksdeutsche from the east as saving them from the fate of ethnic Germans on the Volga.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Condemned the Centre Party, Bavarian People's Party and Catholic Action as political organisations of the clergy and said denominational disputes divide the national community.

notes: Only positions stated in his own words or shown by his own record are answered. The Wannsee minutes were written by Eichmann, so they are a record of the conference Heydrich chaired, not his own text. Statements on topics he never addressed are null. His Protectorate welfare measures (food rations, pensions, unemployment insurance) were tactical wartime moves, so no welfare statements are answered.
